known.title: The candidate refs are benchmarked without omp's web_search, which step 9 adds to the shipped plan reviewer only after shipping, so the measured reviewer is not the shipped one and a5 cannot print nothing
known.locator: Steps, row 3 candidates (line 75), row 4 dev_runs (line 76), row 5 heldout_runs (line 77), row 9 reviewer_tools (line 81); Research, Decisions, decision 7 (line 53); Acceptance, a5 (line 93)
known.summary: prepare.mjs parseVariants loads the agent file of each variant ref, and renderAgent keeps its tools line. At repo_ref, plugins/plan-lifecycle/agents/plan-reviewer.md line 4 lists `Read, Glob, Grep, WebSearch, WebFetch` and no `web_search`. Step 3 writes the candidates as commits from main, steps 4 and 5 measure them, and step 9 adds omp's web_search (decision 7) only after step 6 ships. So the benchmark measures reviewers without the search tool that production gets, and after step 9 the diff of a5 between the winner ref and HEAD holds the tools change, which a5 does not allow. The tools change must come before the candidate refs, so that the measured refs carry it.

known.title: Reviewers get web evidence, but the judge must not use the network and answers unknown for a claim that the snapshot cannot decide, so the wrong-finding bound of decision 5 does not measure the precision of web-based findings
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 1 (line 36), decision 2 (line 37), decision 5 (line 43); Steps, row 1 harness_web (line 73), row 5 heldout_runs (line 77)
known.summary: Decision 1 lets reviewers take official-documentation evidence from the web. At repo_ref, .agents/skills/review-benchmark/references/judge.md line 14 tells the judge not to use the network, and lines 23 and 34 make it answer `unknown` when the snapshot does not decide a claim. score.mjs judgeFindings counts `unknown` apart from `wrong`. A finding whose truth depends on an external manual is then rated unknown, not wrong, so decision 5's bound on wrong findings can pass without the precision that the plan promises. Step 1 harness_web must give both judges official-documentation evidence too, and its Files cell must name references/judge.md.

known.title: Only Ac is measured at effort high, but the rule can recommend high for a D1 or D2 winner whose high-effort result nobody measured
known.locator: Research, Decisions, decision 3 (line 41), decision 5 (line 43); Steps, row 4 dev_runs (line 76), row 5 heldout_runs (line 77), row 6 ship_prompt (line 78)
known.summary: Decision 3 runs only Ac at effort `high` and makes `high` the recommended plan-reviewer effort when Ac-high is not worse than Ac-xhigh. Decision 5 can ship D1 or D2 at xhigh. The benchmark SKILL.md Configurations section and prepare.mjs renderAgent treat the variant and the effort as separate measured combinations, so Ac-high's result does not show the quality of D2 at high. If D2 wins and Ac-high passes, the plan recommends the unmeasured D2-high. The high-effort recommendation must be limited to an Ac outcome, or the winner must be measured at high.

known.title: Steps dev_runs, heldout_runs, and loop_sim all write results.md, but loop_sim has no Depends chain with them and no step owns the shared edit, against the plan contract
known.locator: Steps, row 4 dev_runs (line 76), row 5 heldout_runs (line 77), row 7 loop_sim (line 79), Depends cells
known.summary: Steps 4 dev_runs, 5 heldout_runs, and 7 loop_sim all name .agents/skills/review-benchmark/results.md in their Files cells. Step 7 has Depends `-`, so no chain connects it with steps 4 and 5, and no step owns the shared edit. plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md at repo_ref (lines 73-74) says that two steps that list the same path need a Depends chain between them, or one of them must own the shared edit. Parallel work can then overwrite benchmark tables or the simulation record. loop_sim must come after heldout_runs, or one step must own every results.md edit.

When the tools change lands, before or after the candidate refs, is not part of this decision.

Yolo decision: the code reviewer rates a fault that no current caller, fixture, or documented input reaches as LOW. From code-review round 3, a pass whose open findings are only such LOW findings lands, and the findings go to the run summary and to one follow-up issue. This deliberately changes the rule to repair every finding, and the rule ships only when the loop simulation shows that no known defect escapes.
